sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under conditional unconfoundedness; identification is given and the contribution is limit theory.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with a declared partition into Hall-heavy arms and finite-inverse-moment arms.
sampling_model.overlap: Positivity almost surely; each heavy arm has a uniform second-order Hall lower tail, while each Gaussian arm has a uniformly finite inverse propensity moment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold constrained Bernoulli series likelihood; all scales use an explicit generalized inverse, clipping uses fitted-propensity order statistics with multipliers strictly below one, endpoint scores use nested cross-fitted preliminary quantiles, and the full algorithm is refitted inside each conditionally uniform size-\(m\) subsample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 combines Proposition 8.2's deterministic quadratic Knight-remainder and process limit with Proposition 8.3's finite-dimensional infinitely divisible Lévy score limit for the observed true-propensity clipped fixed-quantile estimator.
A growing series-logit propensity fit yields efficient regular-overlap IPW mean estimation.
A nonparametric estimated-propensity QTE estimator is root-\(n\) normal and efficient under regular overlap.
Adaptive scalar \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) resampling yields inference for mean-type effects under irregular identification.
Thresholded cross-fitted AIPW means admit Gaussian inference under tail-amplified nuisance conditions.
Balance-fitted propensities yield regular limit theory for distributional and quantile treatment effects.

body.tldr: A boundary-adapted growing Bernoulli likelihood can preserve the infinitely divisible clipped-IPW quantile law under Hall weak overlap. For the finite target set, the endpoint law enters only through the pushforward \(H_a=G_a\circ\Psi_a^{-1}\), and the primitive coordinate score modulus yields total-variation convergence of that finite score law without full endpoint outcome-law convergence. The signed-functional expansion derives \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\) for the displayed learner, while a separately defined escape learner proves the amplification order is intrinsically necessary. The fully sample-driven procedure supports heavy, Gaussian, joint unequal-tail, and conditionally uniform refitted arm-vector subsampling with explicit pointwise confidence intervals; the critical fold-labelled Poisson law remains open.

project_justification.gap: The closest weak-overlap QTE theorem uses the observed true propensity. Regular estimated-propensity quantile and series-logit results rely on regular overlap, and weak-overlap nuisance results concern smooth means rather than a moving quantile boundary.
project_justification.niche: A feasible full-population QTE estimator needs a signed likelihood expansion that respects Hall endpoint geometry, convex check loss, clipping drift, and shared folds.
project_justification.fill: The project factors the endpoint Lévy law through the finite score pushforward, derives its total-variation convergence from the primitive coordinate score modulus, derives the amplified transfer condition from a boundary likelihood fit, proves its intrinsic order through an escape perturbation, separates heavy and finite-variance arms, gives a wholly empirical correction, and validates conditionally uniform arm-vector subsampling with explicit pointwise confidence intervals.

body.related_work: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky (2025, arXiv:2506.18215v1) provide the observed true-propensity fixed-quantile result in Theorem 3.1: Proposition 8.2 gives the deterministic quadratic Knight-remainder and process limit, and Proposition 8.3 gives the finite-dimensional infinitely divisible Lévy score limit. On the finite target set used here, that Lévy integrand factors through \(H_a=G_a\circ\Psi_a^{-1}\), so the needed endpoint convergence concerns only nested quantile scores rather than the full conditional outcome law; the paper supplies no feasible propensity-estimation theorem. Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder (2003) inform the growing-likelihood projection under strict overlap. Firpo (2007) informs the regular quantile influence function under strict overlap. Ma and Wang (2020) inform heavy-tail centering for linear IPW means. Heiler and Kazak (2021) inform scalar irregular subsampling. Dorn (2025) informs tail-amplified cross-fit remainder accounting for orthogonal means. Sant'Anna, Song, and Xu (2022) inform regular balance-fitted distributional estimation. None of these informed-by comparisons is presented as a strict theorem extension.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Hall tails alone do not imply uniform propensity learnability, so uniform claims use the boundary-smooth subclass and the proposal proves explicit mixed and two-heavy member neighborhoods. Exactly the finite-variance boundary is excluded. The endpoint restriction controls only the finite nested score vector and does not assert convergence of the full conditional outcome law. The infinitely divisible learned-mark description is not asserted for arbitrary critical-resolution shared-fold learners.
body.honest_scope: The anchor's oracle convex limit is Theorem 3.1 of arXiv:2506.18215v1, with the deterministic process step in Proposition 8.2 and the finite-dimensional Lévy score step in Proposition 8.3. Its finite-quantile Lévy integrand depends on \(G_a\) only through \(H_a=G_a\circ\Psi_a^{-1}\); the derived nested-cell lemma must prove that the primitive score modulus implies total-variation convergence to \(H_a\), and no full endpoint outcome-law convergence is assumed. The boundary likelihood expansion, scale consistency, preliminary-score correction, intrinsic transfer necessity, Gaussian projection, arm recombination, and conditionally uniform refitted pointwise inference remain to be proved. The critical fold law is open. The finite-variance sanity reduction is explicit: on the mixed center, \(h_{0,n}\to2\) and \(\widehat b_{0,n}\to\vartheta_0/2<1/2=\inf_x\pi_0(x)\), so the control clip disappears and the estimator centers at \(q_0\).
